name: Autosomal Dominant Distal Myopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Autosomal Dominant Distal Myopathy

criteria.description: Progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly affecting distal limb muscles
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic mutation in known causative genes (e.g., MYH7, GNE, or others depending on subtype)
Muscle biopsy showing myopathic changes with rimmed vacuoles or other characteristic histopathology
EMG demonstrating myopathic changes with possible fibrillation potentials

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive distal muscle weakness with autosomal dominant family history plus identification of pathogenic mutation in a known causative gene
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Muscle biopsy and EMG findings support diagnosis but are not mandatory if genetic confirmation is available.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically begins in the feet or hands
searchTerms: weakness in hands and feet muscles
difficulty using fingers or toes due to weakness

pathognomonic.symptomName: Muscle atrophy localized to distal extremities
searchTerms: muscle wasting in hands or feet
loss of muscle bulk in extremities

common.symptomName: Foot drop due to anterior tibialis weakness
Mild proximal muscle involvement in later stages
searchTerms: later stage mild weakness near trunk
weakness in upper arms or thighs later on

occasional.notes: Rarely mild distal sensory changes reported

rare.notes: Rarely reported in some genetic subtypes

searchTerms: difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate elevation)
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective fatty replacement and atrophy of distal muscles
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as MYH7, GNE, or other distal myopathy-associated genes
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating myopathic changes with rimmed vacuoles or fiber size variability

distinguishingFeatures: Multisystem involvement including cataracts and cardiac conduction defects
CTG repeat expansion in DMPK gene
Presence of rimmed vacuoles on biopsy
Often associated with Paget disease of bone and frontotemporal dementia

references: Udd B, et al. Distal myopathies: clinical and genetic advances. Neurology. 2015.
Orphanet: Autosomal dominant distal myopathy. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases. 2020.
